# the-internet-herokuapp-com-selenium-tests

A Selenium + JUnit 5 test framework for https://the-internet.herokuapp.com, generated by
[Suite Builder](https://github.com/Ghost-in-the-Kernel-Labs/Ghost-in-the-Kernel-Labs-suite-builder-docs) from a crawl of the site. Its pages and the links between them: [SITE-GRAPH.md](SITE-GRAPH.md).

## Run it

**Lost? Type `crew` in this folder** (or `help`, `suite`, `ask`; in PowerShell `.\crew`, on a Mac or Linux `./crew`): where the suite stands, and a menu of what to do, Claude Code's help among it.

**Stories in Jira? Type `jira login` here, once**: then `jira pull` brings the ready stories in and `jira push` sends each card its tests or its questions. `jira-loop/README.md` explains it, for the BA too.

Needs Java 17+ and Maven. From this folder:

```
mvn test -Dgroups=smoke                every page type loads (start here)
mvn test                               all tests, headless
mvn test -Dgroups=navigation           header, footer and page links land on the right pages
mvn test -Dgroups=menus                links inside dropdown menus
mvn test -Dgroups=links                every address the crawl requested, asked again: target/link-report.md
                                       (fails on one broken since the crawl; 8 broken then, listed)
mvn test -Dheaded=true                 watch it in a browser
mvn test -Dbrowser=firefox             in Firefox, or -Dbrowser=edge, or -Dbrowser=safari; Chrome by default
mvn test -Dgroups=smoke,http           the quick check: every page type opens, every address answers
mvn test -DbaseUrl=https://staging.example.com   against another copy of the site
mvn test -DblockAds=false              with ads (refused by default in Chrome and Edge: they hijack clicks;
                                       for every run, blockAds = false in suite.properties)
mvn test -DtestDelay=1000              a second between tests, on a site you don't own (for every
                                       run, testDelay = 1000 in suite.properties)
mvn test -DstopAfter=0                 every test, even after 5 in a row fail the same way (the run stops
                                       early then, by default, the rest skipped, saying why)
mvn test -DloadBudget=2.5              fail a test whose page takes over 2.5 s to be ready (every page is
                                       timed anyway: target/timings/timings.csv, the slowest listed at the end)
mvn test -Dthreads=4                   four test classes at once, each in its own browser (one at a time unless told)
```

Every setting for every run (the site, the browser, ads, a pause, the waits) is in
`src/test/resources/suite.properties`; a run's first line says which were given, and where from. Every
run writes `target/report.html`: each test, how it went and why, and a failed one's evidence.

Each test prints a line as it starts (`-> SmokeTest: ...`) and how long it took, in a fresh
browser. A test that fails leaves its evidence in `target/failures/<TestClass>/<test>/`: a
screenshot, the page's HTML, its steps and, in Chrome and Edge, the console's errors. Each run
starts clean: the last run's failures move to `target/failures-previous/`, so rerunning one test
keeps the rest of a full run's evidence one run back. `SuiteRulesTest` runs last in a whole run and
reports each of the suite's rules (`SUITE-RULES.md`: how tests are written, and that no generated
file is edited outside its YOURS blocks); a broken rule says where, why the rule exists, and what
to change. It never stops another test: a broken hard or story rule fails the run, an advisory one
is a warning (`target/rules-report.md`). A page gets 30 seconds to load and a check 10
seconds; no test runs longer than 2 minutes.

Chrome, Firefox or Edge must be installed. The first run takes a minute longer: Selenium Manager,
part of Selenium, downloads the driver each browser needs. Before a demo, do that once ahead of
time:

```
mvn test -Dgroups=harness
```

Each page object's `open()` accepts the cookie banner once per test, with its own time limit, and
prints what happened; a banner it can't accept never fails a test by itself (see
`core/CookieBanner`).

## In a pipeline

GitHub, GitLab and Azure: `.github/workflows/suite.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml` (keep yours): `-Dgroups=http,smoke`
on every push, every test nightly in chromium and firefox. The `Dockerfile` runs the suite anywhere. Delete the ones you
don't use: a rebuild leaves them out (an empty file of the same name brings one back).

## Adding elements

Each `<Type>Elements` enum has a marked place for the page's own elements. The section headings
it starts with are the ones every crawled page of that type showed; keep what matters.
Locators from [Selector Grabber](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/gjpelpkcfkikaflgljfgfipblpcmocei) paste
straight in:

```java
SUBMIT_BUTTON(By.xpath("//button[@data-testid='submit']")),
```

Then use them from the Click and Verify actions, and write the tests that need thinking in the
`stories` package.

## Editing, and regenerating

Every file says in its first lines what may be edited. Most are generated with **YOURS** blocks:

```java
    // ==== YOURS (elements): safe to edit; regenerating keeps what is between these lines ====
    SUBMIT_BUTTON(By.xpath("//button[@data-testid='submit']")),
    // ==== END YOURS (elements) ====
```

Regenerating (a new crawl of a changed site) rewrites everything else and keeps what is in the
blocks. Work that no longer has a place (its page type was renamed, say) is moved to
`orphaned/`, never deleted. Files that are wholly yours (`CHANGES.md`, `SmokeTest`, your
story tests) are never touched.

Three blocks start with what the crawl found, for you to change:

- **What proves a page has loaded**: each page class's `PROVES_LOADED` (load-proof). A heading that
  comes and goes (an offer, a banner) makes `isLoaded()` fail: take its line out.
- **A family's examples**: `EXAMPLES` (examples), the pages `open()` and the smoke test use. Put the
  ones you want first.
- **A smoke test**: `SmokeTest` is yours and runs `GeneratedSmokeTest`'s tests; override one there,
  with its `@Test`, to replace it.

Left as they are, a rebuild brings the newer crawl's versions; changed, yours are kept.

## Write a test

The worked example in this suite is `src/test/java/com/herokuapp/theinternet/tests/cases/ForgotPasswordFormTest.java`, a test of ForgotPasswordPage, chosen because its form has the fewest fields of any page's. Open it beside `src/main/java/com/herokuapp/theinternet/tests/pages/forgotpassword/`: it opens ForgotPasswordPage, checks the browser will not send its form empty, fills it through `execute().fillForgotPasswordForm(...)` with test data you can change, and checks each field holds what was typed. Nothing is sent: what happens after Send is the one thing left, and its YOURS block shows the lines to add.

A test of your own is a class in `cases/` that extends `BaseTest`, with JUnit's assertions if you
like. The suite's rules hold it to one thing: it checks something (SUITE-RULES.md).

```java
class HomeHasNewsTest extends BaseTest {
    @Test
    void theHomePageShowsTheNews() {
        new HomePage(driver).open().verify().isLoaded();
        assertTrue(driver.getTitle().length() > 0);
    }
}
```

A test that comes from a story in your tracker is better written as a story (`@Story`, on
`StoryTest`): ai/AI-README.md and stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md say how.

## Working with an AI

With [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), signed in with your own account, run `claude` in this
folder, then:

- `/stories`: the stories in stories/new/ become tests, or come back saying exactly what is needed;
- `/fix-failing`: the last run's failed tests read, the suite's faults fixed, the site's recorded in KNOWN-ISSUES.md;
- `/explain-audit`: the site's audit, explained for its owner, the most serious first.

`ai/AI-README.md` is written for an AI assistant: hand it this folder (zipped is fine), a user story
and the pages the story touches, saved from the browser into `saved-pages/`, and ask for the test.
The crawl this was generated from is in `crawl/`: keep it with the project, and zip the whole
folder when you hand it on.
